correctness.rationale: Tabachnikov's convex bicycle-polygon lemma makes every local \((10,4)\) quadrilateral an isosceles trapezoid. Comparing the trapezoids at indices \(i\) and \(i+5\) forces five-periodic exterior angles; their total then gives opposite side vectors. Central symmetry converts the common side and fourth-diagonal lengths into the exact relation \(r_i+r_{i-1}=C\) for five radius squares. The odd five-cycle forces all radii equal, after which equal side chords force central gaps \(\pi/5\). All boundary cases used in the lifted-angle argument are covered by \(0\le\alpha_i\le\pi\), and no finite experiment substitutes for an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The pair \((10,4)\) is a natural low-complexity member of the published exceptional even-even infinitesimal family, not an arbitrary numerical slice. The theorem resolves the full convex global class at that parameter and explains why second-order infinitesimal flexibility does not integrate to a genuine convex deformation. The two structural mechanisms—forced central symmetry and odd-cycle radius rigidity—are mathematically reusable beyond a one-off computation.
